      <title>Skandalen i Afrikamesterskapet: Senegal får tilbake tittelen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/skandalen-i-afrikamesterskapet_-senegal-far-tilbake-tittelen-1.18087604</link>
      <description>Idrettens voldgiftsrett (CAS) har konkludert med at Senegal gjeninnsettes som vinnere av Afrikamesterskapet i fotball i 2025.
Det har Idrettens voldgiftsrett besluttet, ifølge nyhetskanalen Reuters.
Det er nesten ti måneder siden Senegal forlot banen i protest da vertsnasjon Marokko fikk straffespark på overtid i finalen. Kampen ble stoppet i nærmere et kvarter.
Marokkos Brahim Díaz bommet, og Senegal vant kampen 1-0 etter ekstraomganger.
Det afrikanske fotballforbundet (CAF) ga først ut bøter og utestengelser til Senegal.
I mars ble Senegal fratatt tittelen og Marokko tilkjent 3-0 og seier. Senegals fotballforbund anket saken til CAS.
I oktober ble det gjennomført en høring bak lukkede dører.
Tirsdag kom den endelige kjennelsen i tvisten.
Senegal møtte Norge i gruppespillet i VM i USA i sommer. Der vant Norge 3-2 etter en dramatisk avslutning.
(NTB)</description>

      <title>Ingen utsatt frist for de rødgrønne: Må avklare innen onsdag</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/ingen-utsatt-frist-for-de-rodgronne_-ma-avklare-innen-onsdag-1.18087741</link>
      <description>Finanskomiteen på Stortinget fastholder at fristen for å melde inn politiske forslag og omprioriteringer til statsbudsjettet utløper klokken 10 i morgen, onsdag.
Komiteen hadde et kort møte i dag klokken 13, der det ikke ble gjort endringer i fremdriftsplanen som gjelder for behandlingen av budsjettet på Stortinget.
I praksis betyr dette at budsjettforhandlingene på rødgrønn side må få en avklaring i løpet av dagen, kvelden eller natta. Dermed øker presset på de fem partiene som har forhandlet om statsbudsjettet siden 6. november.
En avklaring må ikke nødvendigvis innebære en budsjettavtale med et avklart flertall bak seg. I fjor la Ap, Rødt og Senterpartiet fram en avtale, som ikke hadde flertall. SV og MDG kom først om bord noen dager senere.</description>

      <description>To personer ble natt til mandag pågrepet av svensk politi i forbindelse med voldshendelsen i Alta søndag morgen, skriver politiet i loggen.

      <title>Karoline Grøtting best av alle på sesongåpningens siste dag – skiskytter imponerte</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/karoline-grotting-best-av-alle-pa-sesongapningens-siste-dag-_-skiskytter-imponerte-1.18086614</link>
      <description>Karoline Grøtting var best av samtlige kvinner under dagens 15 kilometer fristil på Beitostølen.
5 kilometer før mål sto kampen om seieren mellom Grøtting og Kristin Austgulen Fosnæs. Der var det altså Grøtting som til slutt trakk det lengste strået.
Grøtting stod over fredagens 10 kilometer på grunn av magesmerter i et forsøk på å spare seg til dagens distanse.
– Jeg er veldig glad for det nå, sier Grøtting til NRK etter målgang.
Skiskytter Ida Lien var dagens andre startende og gikk i mål til ledelse. Der ble hun værende til Grøtting overtok lederstolen.
Likevel holdt det til 3. plass for skiskytteren.
Heidi Weng vant fredagens 10 kilometer klassisk, men klarte ikke å gjenskape prestasjonen i dag. Allerede ved 6,2 kilometer hadde Weng 17 sekunder opp til teten.
Weng endte på 5. plass, 36 sekunder bak vinner.
Herrene skal ut på sin 15 kilometer klokken 13:00. Den kan du følge på NRK TV.</description>

      <title>Selvik reddet straffe på overtid da Brest vant igjen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/selvik-reddet-straffe-pa-overtid-da-brest-vant-igjen-1.18086449</link>
      <description>Egil Selvik fortsetter å storspille i Brest-målet. Lørdag sikret han 1-0-seier borte mot Strasbourg ved å redde straffespark fem minutter på overtid.
Sraffen ble dømt etter en VAR-gjennomgang av en situasjon der ballen traff armen til Brest-spiller Mama Baldé, men det berget ikke hjemmelaget.
Brest tok ledelsen ved Noah Edjouma i det 22. minutt, etter en svak klarering av keeper Filip Jørgensen. Selvik forsvarte ledelsen med en rekke gode redninger og hjalp laget sitt til den tredje strake seieren i Ligue 1.
Selvik voktet Norges mål i nasjonsligaseieren over Wales for en uke siden, men han måtte overraskende sette seg på benken igjen da Norge knep gruppeseieren med 3-2-seier over Danmark i Parken tirsdag. Da var Ørjan Nyland tilbake i målet. Lørdag satt Nyland på benken for RB Leipzig.
Brest-seieren løftet laget til 6.-plass på tabellen. Strasbourg har bare tre lag bak seg på tabellen.
(©NTB)</description>

      <description>Tre missiler som hadde retning mot Saudi-Arabias hovedstad Riyadh er skutt ned.

      <description>Spillgiganten Rockstar Games knuser alle rekorder, melder Variety.
Allerede på lanseringsdagen omsatte «Grand Theft Auto 6», også kjent som «GTA 6», for 3,79 milliarder dollar.
Det tilsvarer over 37 milliarder norske kroner, og spillet forbigår dermed superheltfilmen «Avengers: End Game» som den største underholdningslanseringen noensinne.
«GTA 6» ble lansert torsdag på PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X og S, i tillegg til at det kan strømmes på Xbox One via Xbox Cloud Gaming.

      <description>Norwegian har teke kontakt med rundt 5000 kundar og bede dei sperre bankkorta sine etter at ein leverandør til nettsidene deira er utsett for datainnbrot, melder NTB.

      <description>Høgsterett har forkasta Frogner-kvinna sin anke om erstatningskrav mot Marius Borg Høiby.
Det var Dagbladet som først omtalte saka.
Høiby blei i Oslo tingrett dømd til å betale Frogner-kvinna 110.000 kroner i oppreising.

Heavy rain is causing overland flooding in parts of the Strathcona Regional District, prompting an advisory for Area D residents Tuesday.

The regional district says water levels may rise quickly in low-lying areas, ditches and near creeks as rainfall continues.

Free sand and sandbags are available at two locations for residents preparing for potential flooding:

  • Oyster River Fire Hall: 2241 Catherwood Road.
  • Campbell River Public Works Yard: Back entrance off Merecroft Road, beside the Campbell River Youth Soccer Association clubhouse.

Residents are asked to bring their own shovels to fill sandbags. Supplies are limited, and people are asked to take only what they need.

The regional district says an additional sandbag distribution site will be established, with details to be announced.

Residents are being advised to move vehicles, valuables and important documents to higher ground, and to clear nearby drains and ditches if it is safe to do so. People should also avoid walking or driving through floodwater and stay away from fast-moving creeks and rivers.

For homes at risk of flooding, officials recommend placing sandbags around the property, particularly in low-lying areas.

Residents should only turn off their home’s main electrical switch if the building is dry. Portable electrical items should be moved somewhere safe, and people should never enter flooded basements or buildings where electrical wires or appliances may be energized.

Updates are available through the Strathcona Regional District website.

Elections BC says recounts are almost complete for two provincial ridings where the number of votes between winning candidates was 50 or fewer.

Recounts for Ladysmith-Oceanside and Kelowna Centre began on Monday, Nov. 23 and are expected to be complete on Tuesday, Nov. 24, according to Elections BC.

In Ladysmith-Oceanside, incumbent NDP candidate Stephanie Higginson was up 50 votes to the Conservatives’ Kris McNichol when polls closed on Oct. 24, with Higginson at 14,354 to McNichol’s 14,304.

In Kelowna Centre, the Conservatives’ incumbent Kristina Loewen was up 43 votes to the NDP’s Loyal Wooldridge, with a total of 11,689 votes to 11,646.

Loewen was also recently named part of Lorne Doerkson’s new cabinet as Minister of Children and Family Development.

RELATED: A list of who is in the new British Columbia Conservative cabinet

Judicial recounts are automatically set when the difference between the top two candidates is 100 votes or fewer.

“Once the judicial recounts are complete, Elections BC will post the results on our website and through a press release to media,” said Elections BC in a statement Tuesday morning.

The B.C. legislature is currently made up of 64 Conservative seats, 27 NDP and two Greens.

It’s a dramatic change from the last legislature, which was made up of 47 New Democrats, 29 Conservatives, two Greens, 13 Independents, and two vacant seats.

To form a majority government in B.C., a party needs 47 of the 93 seats in the Legislative Assembly.

Two Vancouver Island Habitat for Humanity organizations are among five across Canada receiving access to expanded funding for critical home repairs, backed by a $1-million donation from RBC Foundation.

Habitat for Humanity Vancouver Island North, serving Courtenay and Comox, and Habitat Victoria will offer the expanded Critical Repairs program, which helps low-income homeowners afford essential work to keep their homes safe and livable.

The program focuses particularly on older adults aging in place, people living with disabilities, Indigenous Peoples and residents in rural and remote communities.

“What we wanted to do as a pilot was to focus energy on organizations already doing the good work of creating housing security,” Sara Lopez, director of communication and fundraising for Habitat for Humanity Vancouver Island North, told CHEK News.

The goal, added Lopez, was to maximize the impact of the funding by supporting organizations in Campbell River and the Comox Valley already doing important work in their respective communities. The funding helps cover capital improvements, while Habitat also brings its construction team and expertise to complete the work.

Habitat for Humanity says all beneficiaries reported positive outcomes, meaning they were able to remain in safe, quality housing following repairs.

Work completed through the program has included fixing faulty electrical wiring, plumbing problems, damaged roofs and accessibility challenges.

According to a recent report from the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, nearly one million homes across the country need major repairs, representing 6.1 per cent of all homes.

Habitat for Humanity Canada says the program is intended to help people remain safely housed while preserving existing affordable housing.

The pilot was launched with an initial $100,000 donation from RBC Foundation.

The other new participating organizations are Habitat for Humanity Greater Vancouver, Habitat Nova Scotia and Habitat for Humanity Newfoundland and Labrador, while the three Ontario organizations continuing the program are Habitat for Humanity Hamilton, Northumberland County and Windsor-Essex.

The post No tsunami risk to B.C. after 4.2M Alaska earthquake appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

A 4.2 magnitude earthquake rumbled near Anchorage, Alaska on Tuesday morning, and officials say there is no tsunami risk to B.C.

The earthquake occurred at 9:37 a.m. PCT, 10 kilometres west south west of point MacKenzie, Alaska, and 17.6 kilometres away from Anchorage.

The United States Geological Survey has received 750 reports from people saying they felt the earthquake, as of 10:30 a.m.

Emergency Info BC says there is no tsunami risk to the province following the earthquake.

Where does 4.2 magnitude fall on Earthquakes Canada’s scale?

On Earthquakes Canada’s scale, earthquakes with a magnitude between 3.5 and 5.4 are “often felt, but rarely cause damage.”

The next level of those rated under 6.0 will cause “at most slight damage to well-designed buildings. Can cause major damage to poorly constructed buildings over small regions.”

Serious damage isn’t expected until a magnitude 7.0 to 7.9 is reached, while loss of life in areas several hundred kilometres across isn’t expected until a magnitude 8.0-8.9.

A magnitude 9 is the highest on the scale, which Earthquakes Canada calls a “rare great earthquake. Can cause major damage over a large region over 1,000 km across.”

The Vancouver Island ski resort announced its tentative opening date, conditions permitting, alongside a rundown of improvements made during the off-season.

The upgrades range from major chairlift maintenance projects to lodge renovations and new grooming equipment.

“The off-season is a really important time for us because we spend a lot of time doing updates and maintenance projects over the course of the summer,” said resort general manager Mike Manara in a video update.

One of the resort’s largest off-season projects involved replacing the original haul rope and grips on the Hawk chairlift.

The three-kilometre-long steel cable, which carries the chairs around the lift, weighs 21,500 kilograms and measures 42 millimetres in diameter. The scheduled replacement took four days to complete.

Crews also continued the resort’s brush-cutting program and worked to improve drainage across several runs, including Ricks Run, Terrain Park, Whiskey Jack, Lower Westerly, Jacks as well as six kilometres of Nordic terrain.

The resort says the work will help it open terrain with less snow accumulation while providing a better surface for grooming crews.

Inside the resort, Bucks Bar and Grill is getting expanded seating, eight new beer lines, additional TVs and bar games, while the Marmot floor has been upgraded to a more family-friendly space with arcade games and activities.

The opening day announcement comes as a series of storms brings heavy precipitation to Vancouver Island this week, with significant snowfall forecast at higher elevations.

As of 9 a.m. Tuesday, Nov. 24, Mount Washington’s forecast was calling for 38 cm of snow over a 24-hour period, with between 32 and 47 cm forecast from the base to the peak.

The resort has already begun snowmaking operations as it prepares for the upcoming season.

Mount Washington says it will provide further updates as its planned Dec. 11 opening approaches.

A U.S. man had his vehicle impounded for driving more than double the posted speed limit on a B.C. highway earlier this month.

The BC Highway Patrol says an officer spotted a blue 2016 BMW driving “much faster than other traffic” on Highway #99 near Squamish on Nov. 1, around 5:10 p.m.

Using a police laser, the officer reportedly recorded the vehicle travelling at 208 km/h in a 90 km/h zone on the Sea to Sky Highway.

“Even by the standards of the Sea to Sky Highway, this is a terribly dangerous speed,” said Sgt. Michael McLaughlin with the BC Highway Patrol in a release Tuesday. 

The driver was handed a $483 ticket for excessive speeding and had his vehicle impounded for seven days, which also includes tow truck and impound fees.

“Visitors to B.C. are expected to understand and obey our traffic laws. You will not ‘get a break’ just to avoid the inconvenience of losing your vehicle and interrupting your vacation plans,” said McLaughlin.

According to ICBC, speed is a factor in more than 2,400 crashes across the province annually. On average, speed is a factor in 91 deaths in B.C. each year – including nine on Vancouver Island.

“No matter whether it’s locals or visitors, treating the Sea to Sky like the Autobahn has got to stop,” said McLaughlin. “There is a direct correlation between dangerous driving and deadly collisions that shut this highway down for hours at a time.”

Two sailings along the Little River (Comox) – Westview (Powell River) route were also cancelled, the 6 a.m. departing from Comox and the 7:55 a.m. departing from Westview.

  • Whaletown (Cortes Island) – Heriot Bay (Quadra Island)
  • Shingle Spit (Hornby Island) – Gravelly Bay (Denman Island)

BC Ferries says the latest updates on the potential ferry cancellations can be found on its website and X account. People looking for updates by phone can also try calling BC Ferries at 1-888-223-3779.

“We know you have important places to be. We will monitor the weather conditions and will share updates with you as further information becomes available,” said BC Ferries on Tuesday morning.

Wind and rain warnings for Vancouver Island

The ferry cancellations – and potential cancellations – come amid wind and rain warnings across Vancouver Island.

The waters surrounding Vancouver Island were under a marine weather warning on Tuesday morning, with winds forecast between 20 and 60 knots.

A wind warning is in effect for Greater Victoria – particularly near the Juan de Fuca and Haro straits, where southeasterly wind gusts of up to 90 km/h are forecast to blow on Tuesday through Tuesday night.

The wind will remain gusty into Wednesday but dip below the warning criteria throughout the day, before another “potent storm system” arrives Wednesday night, according to Environment Canada.

A similar wind warning with gusts up to 90 km/h is in effect for East Vancouver Island and “exposed coastal areas along the northern portions of the Strait of Georgia, including Quadra, Hornby, and Denman Islands” on Tuesday.

In the North Island, Environment Canada is warning of wind gusts up to 110 km/h on Tuesday morning, before the gusts ease later in the day.

Vancouver Island residents are being warned to prepare for potential power outages.

Meanwhile, a rainfall warning is in effect for West Vancouver Island and Inland Vancouver Island, where 100 to 200 millimetres of rain is expected to fall Tuesday, with higher amounts in certain spots.

Like the wind, the rain is expected to ease on Wednesday morning before another stormy system arrives late Wednesday afternoon, bringing with it another round of precipitation and wind.

Locals should watch for potential washouts and water pooling on roads.

More than 5,500 BC Hydro customers are without power Tuesday morning as heavy rain and strong winds continue to sweep Vancouver Island.

Environment Canada has maintained several yellow wind and rainfall warnings across the Island, with wind gusts of up to 90 km/h forecast for Greater Victoria and torrential rain expected to continue in western and inland regions.

The weather agency says conditions should ease Wednesday morning before another powerful storm moves into the region later in the day.

As of around 8 a.m. Tuesday, BC Hydro was reporting 22 outages affecting around 5,500 customers across Vancouver Island.

Among the hardest-hit communities was Ucluelet, where more than 2,000 customers were affected by two outages, including one caused by a downed wire.

In Campbell River, more than 1,200 customers were without power, with the largest outage caused by a downed power pole.

More than 1,100 customers in Nanaimo were also affected by an outage, the cause of which remains under investigation.

Crews have been assigned to or are already on scene at several of the outages, many of which began in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

Rain and wind warnings

Rainfall warnings remain in effect for western and inland Vancouver Island, as well as eastern Vancouver Island from Duncan to Nanaimo and Courtenay to Campbell River.

Environment Canada is forecasting rainfall amounts of 100 to 200 millimetres across western and inland regions, with locally higher amounts possible.

Meanwhile, strong southeasterly winds gusting up to 90 km/h are expected to continue throughout Tuesday and into the night in parts of Greater Victoria near the Juan de Fuca and Haro straits.

Wind warnings also remain in effect for northern Vancouver Island and eastern Vancouver Island between Nanoose Bay and Campbell River.

While Islanders can expect a brief reprieve from the stormy conditions Wednesday, it won’t last long.

“Rainfall rates will ease Wednesday morning but another potent storm arrives late Wednesday afternoon bringing a new round of significant precipitation and strong winds,” Environment Canada said in an updated warning Tuesday.

In Greater Victoria, winds are expected to gradually ease throughout Wednesday before picking up again Wednesday night.

The BC River Forecast Centre also issued a high streamflow advisory Monday for northern, eastern, western and central Vancouver Island, warning that already saturated soils could contribute to rapidly rising river levels.

King tides and storm surges, peaking Tuesday, could further exacerbate high water levels near river mouths.

Residents are being urged to stay away from fast-flowing rivers, avoid flooded roads, secure loose outdoor objects and prepare for further potential disruptions to transportation and utilities.
